# SPSC RingBuffer benchmarks, 2026-11-01

Latency of `RingBuffer` (`spsc.hpp`) on the Intel box, driven by real NASDAQ ITCH traffic replayed over UDP.

## Summary

- **`alignas(64)` on `_head` and `_tail` is worth keeping.** Without it, typical push-to-pop time rises from 114 to 127 ns (+12%) and p99.99 from 555 to 693 ns (+25%).
- **Only the last two runs' tails can be trusted, and only the last run's maximums.** Harness artefacts dominated the tails in the earlier runs. p50 and p99 are usable in all runs.
- **The queue was never saturated.** It was nearly empty throughout, so these results don't show the cost of false sharing under sustained contention.

## Reference numbers

Use this table as the baseline for later comparisons: fully fixed harness, `SPEED=100`. Each cell is the median of 5 runs, with the range across those runs in brackets, in nanoseconds.

| Row | Percentile | With `alignas(64)` (`7fdb41b`) | Without (`7d1222f`) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Push to pop (`e2e` mode) | p50 | 114 (105–115) | 127 (117–129) | **+12%, no overlap** |
| | p99 | 274 (264–281) | 281 (262–289) | No clear change |
| | p99.9 | 344 (337–374) | 396 (354–428) | +15%, slight overlap |
| | p99.99 | 555 (536–643) | 693 (580–718) | +25%, slight overlap |
| | max | 12,223 (4,310–17,144) | 15,605 (2,524–36,887)* | Noise |
| `push` (`percall` mode) | p50 | 26.7 (23–27) | 28.4 (28–30) | One clock step |
| | p99 | 53.5 (48–55) | 55.1 (55–58) | One clock step |
| | p99.9 | 120 (117–122) | 137 (137–140) | **+14%, no overlap** |
| | p99.99 | 164 (142–177) | 170 (164–184) | No clear change |
| | max | 371 (331–451) | 406 (368–17,371) | Noise |
| `pop` returning a tick (`percall` mode) | p50 | 68.5 (67–68) | 70.2 (65–72) | Overlaps |
| | p99 | 142 (140–149) | 152 (145–155) | +7%, overlaps |
| | p99.9 | 169 (167–174) | 175 (174–180) | +4%, touching |
| | p99.99 | 200 (200–204) | 207 (202–212) | +3%, overlaps |
| | max | 5,173 (4,554–15,547) | 15,288 (4,741–32,293) | Noise |

\* The range excludes one corrupted sample; see [Known issues](#known-issues).

Timer overhead (21.7 ns) is already subtracted from `push` and `pop`. Push-to-pop in `e2e` mode has no timers around the calls, so it's the fairest comparison. `percall` slows both threads, so its own push-to-pop figure (219 ns p50) isn't comparable.

## Setup

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Machine | Intel Core i7-3635QM (Ivy Bridge), 4 cores, SMT off, Turbo off, about 2.4 GHz, `performance` governor |
| Kernel and compiler | 7.0.0-42-generic; g++-15 15.2.0, `-O2 -march=native -DNDEBUG` |
| Isolation | `isolcpus=2-3 nohz_full=2-3 rcu_nocbs=2-3 irqaffinity=0-1` |
| Cores | Sender on 1 (not isolated), producer on 2, consumer on 3 |
| Traffic | `12302019.NASDAQ_ITCH50`, 15:50:00 to about 16:00:30, 18,228,261 messages over loopback |
| Ticks | 715,724 per run: `E`, printable `C`, `P` and `Q` only (3.9% of messages) |
| Queue | `RingBuffer<Stamped, 65536>`, 40-byte slots (32-byte `Tick` plus an 8-byte timestamp) |
| Design | 2 variants, alternating, 5 rounds per variant in each mode, 20 replays per run |
| Socket | `rmem_max` 4 MB; no buffer drops in any run where drops were counted |

All 120 replays were valid: 0 packets lost, 0 full pushes, and message, tick and share counts matched the sender. The kernel logs showed no memory or machine-check errors. One `nouveau` GPU fault at 20:04:26 killed the terminal app's graphics channel at about the start of the baseline's `percall` mode. That mode's results fall within the same ranges.

### False sharing at each load

Push to pop, `e2e` mode, median ns, with `alignas(64)` → without:

| Run | Speed | p50 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 10 | 112 → 127 (+13%) | 302 → 324 (+7%) |
| 3 | 100 | 102 → 130 (+28%) | 279 → 296 (+6%) |
| 4 | 0 | 104 → 127 (+23%) | 272 → 291 (+7%) |
| 5 | 100 | 112 → 129 (+15%) | 272 → 279 (+2%) |
| 6 | 100 | 114 → 127 (+12%) | 274 → 281 (+2%) |

The p50 cost is 13–28 ns, and it points the same way in every run. The two `SPEED=100` runs on fixed harnesses give a 13–17 ns cost, so the 28 ns in run 3 is probably on the high side.

## What changed the tails

| Row, with `alignas(64)`, `SPEED=100` | Run 3: original | Run 5: queue pre-touched | Run 6: histogram too |
|---|---|---|---|
| Push to pop p99.9 | 2,145 | 364 | 344 |
| Push to pop p99.99 | 14,950 | 548 | 555 |
| Push to pop max | 60,837 | 83,994 | 12,223 |
| `push` p99.99 | 2,628 | 172 | 164 |
| `push` max | 15,453 | 419 | 371 |

1. **First-touch page faults in the queue.** The queue is a static object in `.bss`, so its 640 pages weren't mapped until first written. A separate test measured 640 slow pushes in the first lap (about 1.9 µs each, up to about 6.9 µs) and none in later laps. That's 0.089% of ticks, just inside the 0.1% that p99.9 looks at. One push/pop lap before traffic removed them (`7c6159c`).
2. **A memory allocation on the consumer thread.** The first sample over about 3.4 µs allocated histogram storage mid-run. Allocating and mapping that storage up front took the `e2e` maximum from 75–94 µs to about 12–16 µs, and consumer page faults to 0 (`64bc5dd`).

## Other findings

- **Tails drift between sessions**, and p50 is much steadier. Run variants alternately in one session rather than against stored numbers.
- **Flat out only reached about 2.1 times `SPEED=100`.** There were no buffer drops, so the sender appears to be the limit, at about 149,000 packets/s. Ticks still averaged about 4 µs apart and the consumer spent nearly all its time polling an empty queue.
- **`rmem_max` at 4 MB wasn't a limit** at any speed tested.
- **`bench-compare.py` missed a real change** at 5 rounds: tied samples kept fully separated runs at p = 0.0117, above its limit of 0.01. It now treats non-overlapping samples as different (`e7338f7`). Run 2's verdict came from per-run values for this reason.

## Known issues

- **A corrupted maximum.** One sample in run 6 (`7d1222f`, round 2, `e2e`) reported 7.7 × 10¹⁸ ns. That's almost exactly 2⁶⁴ clock counts, so `now - v->tsc` went slightly negative and wrapped as unsigned. Unfenced `rdtsc` reordering or clock offset between cores could explain it; this hasn't been tested. It can only corrupt that run's maximum, so percentiles aren't affected. Not fixed.
- **Remaining maximums of about 4–37 µs** in `e2e` and `pop` are unexplained.
- **`pop_empty` is at the timer's limit**, and differences of one clock step (1.67 ns) can be flagged by the script. Ignore those.

## Limits of these results

- The queue carries executions only. Book updates (`A`, `F`, `X`, `D`, `U`) would raise its traffic about 25 times and enlarge its slots, so the baseline would need recording again.
- Because the queue stays nearly empty, these numbers mostly describe a burst going through an idle queue. A saturation test needs a mode with no network.
- Why `pop` costs more than `push`, and why `e2e` shows false sharing more clearly than `push`, are explanations that haven't been measured. The likely factors are the store buffer hiding part of `push`'s cost and `pop` pulling cache lines from the producer's core.

## Reproducing

Raw results are on the Intel box in `~/Documents/dev/profiling/bench/`, one folder per run: `spsc-baseline-`, `spsc-falsesharing-`, `spsc-falsesharing-speed100-`, `spsc-falsesharing-speed0-`, `spsc-pretouch-speed100-` and `spsc-prefault-speed100-`, each ending `20261101`.

Run 6, from `src/feed-handler/claude` at `64bc5dd` or later:

```bash
export CXX=g++-15 FROM=15:50:00 SPEED=100 ROUNDS=5 MESSAGES=18228261
export ITCH_FILE=~/Documents/dev/profiling/data/itch/12302019.NASDAQ_ITCH50
MODE=e2e     ./spsc-bench.sh git:7fdb41b git:7d1222f
MODE=percall ./spsc-bench.sh git:7fdb41b git:7d1222f
```

`spsc-bench.sh` clears its results folder at the start of each run, so copy the results out between modes.
